answer: Each agent allocates 64 GB of dedicated RAM to construct a cedar trie, hashing memory nodes across an unswappable physical ridge via Blake3. At epoch zenith, verifiers issue latency-bound read challenges against the committed root. The probed node must return state leaves within 15 milliseconds. Late responses or checksum mismatches burn a 5,000-coin bond and drop peer identity. Sybils cannot virtualize memory without failing the latency window; faking thirty nodes demands 1.92 TB physical DDR5 costing over $6,000.
